page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 CPU architecture, paired with 512.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, positioning it for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM capacity relative to compute resources.

This instance type does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through attached network storage volumes. Additionally, the c4a-highmem-64 does not feature any integrated graphics processing units and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture typically offers a favorable performance-per-watt and resource density profile compared to traditional architectures, particularly for memory-bound applications. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource contention. This server type is suited for workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, enterprise applications, and data processing pipelines that require a high memory footprint without requiring specialized hardware acceleration.
